name: Flooring

seo.title: Top-Rated Flooring in Sioux Falls, SD
seo.description: Compare flooring companies in Sioux Falls, SD. Browse hours, phone numbers, reviews, and a local guide to choosing the right floor for your home.

heroImageAlt: Freshly refinished light hardwood floors in a bright, empty room with white trim and natural window light.
intro:
Flooring is one of the bigger decisions you make in a home, and in Sioux Falls it comes with some specific considerations. Clay soil under many older neighborhoods shifts with the freeze and thaw cycle, which can stress concrete slabs and affect what flooring performs well over time. Winters bring tracked-in moisture, road salt, and grit, and summers can run humid enough to make solid hardwood move.

A good local flooring company will walk you through how each material holds up under those conditions, not just show you what looks good in a showroom. Ask about installation methods, subfloor prep, and what warranties actually cover in real-world use.
tips: Ask whether the company handles subfloor repairs themselves or subcontracts that work, since a bad subfloor will ruin any material you put on top of it.
Request samples to live with at home for a few days before you commit, because showroom lighting and your own rooms read very differently.
Ask specifically how the product handles moisture, since Sioux Falls basements and main floors near entryways take on real humidity swings through the year.
Get a written estimate that separates material costs from labor so you can compare quotes from different companies on equal terms.

faqs.q: What is the best flooring for a Sioux Falls basement?
faqs.a: Luxury vinyl plank is the most common choice for Sioux Falls basements because it handles moisture and temperature swings better than hardwood or laminate. Engineered hardwood is sometimes used but needs careful attention to humidity levels. Ask any installer about the specific moisture readings in your basement before choosing a product.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to install hardwood floors in Sioux Falls?
faqs.a: Prices vary depending on wood species, board width, finish type, and the condition of your existing subfloor, so there is no single number that applies to every job. The best approach is to get at least two or three written quotes from local companies that include a subfloor inspection. Ask each company to break out material and labor separately so the quotes are easy to compare.

faqs.q: Does clay soil in Sioux Falls cause flooring problems?
faqs.a: Clay soil can shift with freeze and thaw cycles, which sometimes causes concrete slabs to crack or heave slightly over time. This movement can telegraph through rigid flooring like tile or hardwood if the subfloor is not properly prepared. A good installer will check your slab for level and stability before recommending a product.

faqs.q: How long does flooring installation take?
faqs.a: Most average-sized rooms take one to two days once materials have been acclimated to your home, but whole-home projects can run a week or more depending on subfloor work and the number of transitions involved. Acclimation time for hardwood can add several days before installation even begins. Ask your installer for a realistic project timeline in writing before you schedule.

faqs.q: Is carpet or hard flooring better for Sioux Falls winters?
faqs.a: Carpet holds heat better underfoot and can be more comfortable in bedrooms during cold months, but hard flooring near entryways is easier to clean after snow, slush, and road salt get tracked in. Many Sioux Falls homeowners use a combination, with hard flooring in high-traffic entry areas and carpet in living spaces and bedrooms. Think through how each room gets used before deciding.

faqs.q: Do I need to remove old flooring before new flooring goes in?
faqs.a: It depends on the material and the condition of what is already there. Some products can be installed over existing flooring if it is flat, secure, and in good shape, but adding height can create problems at doorways and transitions. Ask your installer to assess the existing floor in person rather than making that call before they have seen it.
